title: Small diagrams of module sheaves form a Grothendieck category
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site (small in a universe containing the values of all sheaves), let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of rings, not necessarily commutative, and let $J$ be a small category in that universe. Let $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ denote the category of sheaves of left $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The category $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\Mod(\mathcal O))$, whose objects are functors and whose maps are natural transformations, is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]: it is abelian, has all small colimits, its filtered colimits are exact, and it has a generator.
